content.label: I bought this to go with the companion iPad app and they work really well together. It was well worth the money invested and will pay for itself many times over with time efficiencies gained. Easy to learn and my knowledge improved with use. Recommended.
If would add reminders for the checklist, and two reminders before an event, I would have given 5 star. Very good interface but not very practical without these reminders.

I do love this app so bought both the macOS and iOS versions. They look gorgeous and manage to strike the balance between simplicity and complexity. Functions make sense and you manage to Get Things Done.

So what’s not to like?

One small issue. I plan my tasks the night before where I prioritise the majority of my work related and a small number of personal tasks during the day. However, there is no way to schedule tasks for the next evening unless you stay up until after midnight or do this in the morning.

One big issue. I love my iPhone and MacBook. They are my workhorses at home. But, at work, I’m using CentOS with a Windows 10 VM. I understand that an app for other operating systems would be a big ask but I don’t understand why there’s not a web version?

I would love to continue being productive at work without having to use my phone when I have a big screen, keyboard and mouse. I’m aware that I can email new tasks to myself but I’m referring to the ability to view all projects and tasks on my big screen. 

It’s 2019 guys, you can do this!
Serves it’s purpose very well - simple, well thought-through and handy

I don’t normally write reviews, and I certainly don’t normally spend a tenner on an app...but I am so chuffed with Things. 

Yes, you could get results using Apples notes, reminders and calendar. 
But that’s a real flaff compared to this single app. 

Clean, simple and effective. 
In just 20 minutes I started to feel I was getting things (no pun intended) in order and could feel my mind clearing. 

Top marks 👍

title.label: Where has Things been all my life!?

content.label:
I don’t write that many reviews so an App has to be quite exceptional for me to spend a bit of time doing so... and Things is exceptional.. and more!

After struggling by with Apple Reminders and other inferior to do lists for years a friend said for me to try this... and I was hooked.

As a busy engineer I run many projects simultaneously and this is the app I now use. Simple to use, powerful and reliable.

I also use it for my to dos around the home so please don’t think it’s all business.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s not cheap and the iPad and Mac versions are quite an extra cost but it’s a small price for perfection.
Easy to use immediately...simple but so effective in GSD. I just went through the full tutorial and it’s even better than I thought. Use this every day now!

For me the real reason I love this app is it’s Apple Watch complication. It does what no other reminders app does and that’s show you a constant reminder throughout the day. Every other app wants you to set a time or date. 
One request would be for the watch complication to change the displayed reminder on each glance at the watch face.
That what you can set a list of stuff you need to do that day but none of them at specific times and every glance at the watch your reminded of a different task.

I am in awe of this application. Paired with Things on all my iOS devices and my Mac (yeah, I'm one of those folk!), Things has really revolutionised my habits. Once upon a time I continuously put off completing tasks, and was crazy forgetful about everything. Now, I simply rely upon Things to remember for me, and to prod me into doing stuff on time.

It took a while to actually form the habit of listing my to-dos in the app, but once I started, it became almost automatic. Things has also become so beautiful over the years, especially the new Dark Mode. The design and intuition that’s gone into it is stunning. I love it, and recommend it to everyone. One thing I would really like to draw attention to is the sync speed between devices — it is SO fast. I honestly don’t know how they manage it. 

It's only now that I'm writing a review (something I never do!), but as a result I can vouch that Things is one of the best apps I've used over a multi-year period. To think that the team are still adding small quality of life features every now and then! I think it’s perfect already, but you can be sure they’ll think of something.
Everything I need is here and the design is refined enough to not get over complicated even with some very powerful tools
Beautiful design inside, but sadly the app icon itself is quite ugly when sitting next to other apps. Needs to be more minimalist and clean.

title.label: Good but not as user friendly as you’d expect

content.label: This is a handy app especially as it can link to Apple Watch and you can add reminders that way. However, it’s not always easy to navigate. How do you delete a recurring item permanently? All it seems to do it delete it for that week. After trying seemingly every option I can access I still can’t find it, meaning I can’t permanently delete a reminder for a task which I no longer need to do, reducing the usefulness of the app. It needs to be easier to do simple things.
Would love if I could default to intrusive reminder when creating a task with due date rather than having to manually specify to alert me, on each task.

title.label: The best for organising your life

content.label:
I love Things3 and have been using it on all of my devices. It is highly customisable has a very elegant design. 

Feature request:

I’d love a view called ‘This Week’ which looks like a calendar view and shows you all your tasks for the week. For me, this would make the app the ultimate tool for organising. I have ADHD and right now I also need to look at a calendar to visualise my time.

Better features for visualisation would be amazing.

I have tried a few task managers, thinking there must be some free software that could do what I wanted. I tried a number of different ones but they all lacked one thing or another. I balked at Things 3 due to the price, but after being frustrated by the other options I decided to give it a go. I admit, the team at Cultured Code have created the perfect app which is worth the money. You certainly get what you pay for. Well done, everyone.

Not the best todo app out there and it’s way overpriced,

I was hoping it could interact with the iOS reminders app but it will only import the items and then deletes them from the reminder app after they are imported.

I’m also disappointed that you have to pay another £19.99 if you want to use this basic app on your iPad.

Save your money, there are lots of free apps out there that are way better than this.
Things should have a notepad I need a notepad aswel as a planner

title.label: Well thought out, but (still) not perfect yet

content.label:
(Note, I never used earlier generations of things so I'm coming to this version fresh)

I like the design - you've clearly put a lot of thought and work into meeting people's needs while also keeping it simple. It shows, and deserves to be highlighted.

I've found a couple of niggles though:

1. The use of space is a bit too lavish in some places.
Overall, I like what you've done in giving each task enough space to separate it from its neighbours, but a checklist is a single thing, and I think the items should be displayed closer together to express that unity.

2. It could do with templates that aren't repeating tasks / projects.
I have checklists for when I'm going on trips, etc. I want a way to create a project and popular it with the relevant item. For now I've created a "Templates" Area and put things there that I can duplicate then move to where I want them. Trouble is, these things then show up under Anytime.

No joke. I have over 250 apps. This one is the best. 

Only downside is that it can load slower when you have put a lot of items in.
When Things 3 works it is excellent but the app constantly freezes, not ideal when you want to update something quickly.
This app really has changed my life...highly recommend it!

title.label: Very nice app, but extra ££ for each platform

content.label: Lovely app, clean and simple but very powerful. Given the cost of the app, I think it’s really stingy to not include the iPad app. I’d expect to have to pay once for an iOS version. I would be prepared to pay again for MacOS version.
The app is just perfect!

Awesome app, organised us instantly!
The best To Do app out there.
I love the way the items on the To Do list roll over to the next day if the tasks are not done on the specified day.
A great app backed up by an excellent, speedy customer service.

title.label: Simply the best... as Tina Turner would say!

content.label: Things has been my number one app for the last 4 years! I’ve tried the others and none of them compare! The iOS and MacOS versions are pretty much same and it’s so natural to go between each. Amazing app!

Why does it take so long to open? A good 5 seconds on my iPhone XS....have never understood why people get do excited about this application, it is overpriced and does not do not much over and above what list managers do for a quarter of the price. 
I always worry about an application when you read reviews and it is full of "beautiful design" comments, like that is an excuse for charging to much and offering limited functionality.....not in my book  it ain't.

title.label: App could be great but takes too long to load

content.label: Whenever I want to use it, it takes ages to load up anything.

title.label: This is a great app but not quite perfect

content.label:
Firstly, I recommend this app. If you’re using it for yourself as an individual or self employed professional on your own it’s fab. I have it for both iPhone and iPad and it’s great (I don’t have a Mac). 

So I did have three things but the excellent customer support told me how to use the slightly hidden intelligent language parsing in the date picker. So two of three minor issues solved. Great first class customer support too. 
So that leaves the most annoying issue for me, which is task order in the today list, or the upcoming list for that matter. There should be the choice to order these by time of reminder as well as date (in the upcoming list’s case it does group tasks by due day but not reminder time). It especially annoys me on the today list. Just an option in settings to turn on sorting by reminder time would be perfect for me. Personally I’d like to have no due time tasks first in today then tasks with a due time below in order of due time getting later towards the bottom of the list. Having to keep manually reordering things each day is a little tiresome. It’s good that I’m reviewing all the tasks each morning but still, some automation for list order would be super useful and would personally save me that extra little bit of time. 

But other than this grumble I love the app. Fav task management app that I use daily for personal and work tasks. The Apple Watch app integration is great too.
This app is perfect if you like using your Apple Watch to see reminders/checklist as a complication. Easily the best third party Apple Watch app out there

title.label: Best of the Bunch and improving

content.label:
I have tried a lot of task managers but Things 3 is my ‘go to’ app, particularly when combined with Bear for notes etc. 

Tags and data manipulation is excellent with huge flexibility to meet your needs as you require and not forced down a particular way of working. I use David Allen’s GTD to great effect with Things 3 - a huge leap forward over previous iterations. 

Developer is responsive and whilst there is an up front cost, this is significantly less that the subscription fees I am paying with other similar apps. 

Keep up the good work.

title.label: The one, the only, the mighty Things.

content.label:
Been using Things on and off since v1.

It’s the best of the best but if you want to have the suite across an iPhone, iPad and Mac get ready to spend a pretty penny.

That said it’s still much, much better than paying through the nose every month for the rest of eternity.

The screenshots may give the illusion of something pretty basic but it’s a powerhouse.

title.label: How can GTD be this fun?

content.label: Things is a marvel. It makes life management a breeze and more than that, a joy! I couldn’t imagine how v2 could be improved but v3 is just extraordinary. The boring side of lists and projects move to the background and the gorgeous UI and completely intuitive workflows make Things unprecedented in its field. Sure it’s not cheap, thank goodness for that as one gets what one pays for. Keep up the work that sets you apart. Thanks for making a suite of one app, that doesn’t have me resenting getting things done!

title.label: It's great, but no non-mac support

content.label:
I bought this app as I was in search of a great to-do list and this has great reviews. It was, hand on heart, the most expensive app I've ever bought but I felt it would be worth it. I can confirm it's a well designed app that is quite easy to use, 

HOWEVER,

1. They only support Apple devices. So if you only have an iPhone but otherwise use PCs you have no other way of accessing your list. Not even a web interface. This is a giant pain not only for easy accessibility but also it's often easier to see things on a bigger screen to see the bigger picture, move things around, plan, etc. I'd rather use my phone for quick entry and my PC to categorise, plan, set deadlines, etc.

2. I can't find a way to pull up a list of ALL my outstanding items. Maybe not something most people would want but I find it useful. 

So for me it's just not the app I need. I hope someone else finds this info useful before they drop a fiver on an app with limited portability.
It’s good, but can you add the ability to empty logbook on iPhone?

title.label: Great app; use it every day

content.label:
Things simply keeps my life organised. I love the Integration with Apple's Reminders and Calendars. Through Siri I can easily input new tasks on the fly. 

The today view (opened quickly with Siri shortcuts) nicely shows all things to be done today underneath a list of Calendars events. 

The Apple watch app is great at the supermarket where the shopping list can be displayed and checked off. I've got headings setup based on the supermarket's aisles so the items needed are in the correct order. 

There's not a lot I would change. A nice addition would be a quick link to today's events in the Calendar app with a tap on the events list in Things' today view, if this is technically possible. 

Throughout recommended!
I routinely use Things 3 for basic organisation and find it excellent but I’m mystified why some people treat it as something of great brilliance.
Beautifully done app! Well designed and developed. Must have!

I’ve been using Things for years. I love that I can use it across multiple platforms (iPad etc.) and that it is intuitive to create and keep up to date with various to do lists. The perfect personal organiser app
Really good tool to make life more efficient. A bit pricey but at least there is no subscription fee.

I really wanted to like this app, and did so for a while. But the price is too high to get it on my Mac and all my devices. Having built up several hundred tasks and notes across many projects, it was only then I discovered that I can’t export all the data, unless done literally sharing copy and pasting *every* *single* *task*. Support confirmed this. 

For a professionally-priced app, this is simply not good enough.

Really nice design! I'll look forward to future updates. There website has lots of cool information too. You guys should add your trailer video to the App Store because I think it was so well done- made me excited to do stuff lol- and I think it would bring in more potential buyers.

Feature Request: Subtasks Visible at all times option in settings.

Feature Request: Adding Tags to multiple tasks at the same time.

Feature Request: Dark UI Theme.

Update: new dark mode looks awesome! Cheers for adding that!

title.label: Disappointed that you need to pay again for iPad app

content.label: Decent app however I’m really disappointed that you have to pay again to use on iPad (or if purchased on iPad then pay on iPhone) there are alternatives.

I was weary to buy Things 3 everywhere (iPhone, iPad, Mac). I got lucky and grabbed Things 2 when it was free then took the plunge when Things 3 just came out...

Let me say it's worth every single pence I've paid. My life is calmer and I'm on top of everything I should be, due to how fast, simple and clear it is to use Things 3. 

I've loved every minute with the app, but now, with the Black Theme on iPhone X, they made something perfect. That's it. Endgame. This is your app if you want to organise your life.

I rarely write reviews but this app has honestly transformed the way I think! It has helped add so much organisation to my life where I don’t forget things I would usually and I’m super productive and driven to get my to do list for the day completed everyday! 

Honestly if you’re having problems with productivity there is no better app!!
Yip, they’ve just knocked it out the park! 3.8 at last gives us the same look and feel as MacOS and it’s brilliant. Great work guys!
When I wake up the to do app badge notifications icons aren’t shown until I enter the app then come out, nor are the things shown on the widget until I go into the app then come out. Please fix.

I’ve used a range of to-do apps over the years eventually settling on one that worked well across platforms and was free (and supported moveable sub tasks). However, Things is functionally richer with a more enjoyable interface. It does what I need for simple tasks as well as for more complex situations. 

In particular I like being able to slide up the blue + symbol and add a task to where I want (eg on a particular day in the upcoming calendar view, or to a particular project (sliding up the + in the anytime view). 

Also handy is being able to do a voice input to add a task to Things using my Apple Watch.

Why is there no functionality for sharing lists or to-do’s with other Things users?! Seems ludicrous for such an amazing app. This is an absolute essential that is sorely missed in this otherwise perfect app. Team Things, please please PLEASE sort this out!!

Things 3 has got the crowd buzzing and long may it remain so but..... a little less developer greed and a little more strategic thinking and the boys and girls at Cultured Code GmbH could be giving each other a Christmas bonus for years to come. Simply halve the cost of Things 3 on all platforms and watch those people who think you’re too expensive on Mac and iPad snap it up across all systems just because they like that sort of synergy. You’ll sell more than enough to compensate and align yourself to at least 3 times as many customers ...... The current short sighted greediness is keeping people away. Shame because it’s a very very good system when you use it well.
